CyanogenMod 12.1 nightly, sans gapps for privacy, on Nexus 6.

I'm all for privacy, but with the granular controls (ie turn off location services/disable access to other things) can't you better manage even the GApps? What are your alternatives for the defaults that GApps provides? Are you just running with the CM alternatives?

The granular controls are helpful in containing what the Google apps (or any others) can access, but the issue is that Google apps package is so much more than a collection of userspace apps (maps, gmail, etc). When you install Google apps, you get the Google play services package, which is a proprietary binary. Lots of Play Store apps rely on Play Services, and the service is always running, as it ties deeply into the OS itself. (One such example: Play Services handles the WiFi enhanced geolocation service on the device. Your location is resolved using this API, which then transmits location metadata to Google.) There are a lot of convenient API's provided via Play Services, but since its proprietary I chose not to have this running as part of my OS.

As for alternative apps, I find most of what I need on F-Droid. The only thing I truly moss having is YouTube, which doesn't seem to allow 3rd party apps. Web version works but is clunky.
